**Not ready to publish.**

**Product label check**

| Product | Label | Hands-on claims |
|---|---|---|
| Pebblebrook subscription | **Not given** (Owned, Tried or Wishlist?) | "the easiest to pause", "the tins are lovely" |

I can't assume the writer owns or has tried it. If it's Wishlist, both hands-on claims have to go. If it's Owned or Tried, the post should say how long they've used it.

**Problems**

1. **No affiliate disclosure.** This is an affiliate post, but nothing at the top declares it before the first link. The link ("You can find it here.") also has no "Affiliate link" label next to it. Both are required.
2. **"Easiest to pause" is an unsupported comparison.** Our policy only backs "Subscribers can pause or cancel any time". Ranking it against three other services is a superlative we can't prove, and the draft names none of the other three. If the writer really did compare them, the post should say what they did on each service. Otherwise, use the allowlisted wording.
3. **"I've tried four tea subscriptions this year" is unverified.** It's a hands-on claim with no detail. Confirm it's true and name the four, or cut it.
4. **Gifted or paid status is unknown.** If Pebblebrook sent the tins or paid for the post, it must open with "Gifted" or "Ad" before anything else. Please confirm.

**Suggested fix, pending the writer's answers**

> Affiliate link: this post contains an affiliate link to Pebblebrook Tea Co.
>
> [Label: e.g. "I've been a subscriber for X months."] Subscribers can pause or cancel any time, and I found pausing simple: [what they actually did]. The tins are lovely: [specific detail, e.g. size or design]. Affiliate link: [link]

Sam needs to approve it before it goes out, as with all public content.

```json
{"issues": [
{"quote": "I've tried four tea subscriptions this year.", "type": "missing_disclosure"},
{"quote": "You can find it here.", "type": "missing_disclosure"},

{"quote": "I've tried four tea subscriptions this year.", "type": "other"},

], "publish": false}
```
